MATHEMATICS — TERMLY EXAM #17 (TERM 2)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Simplify 8y + 2 − 3y. (1 mark)
   A. 11y + 2
   B. 5y − 2
   C. 5y + 2
   D. 7y

2. If m = 7, what is the value of 6m? (1 mark)
   A. 67
   B. 42
   C. 13
   D. 1

3. Simplify 3m + 2o + m + 4o. (1 mark)
   A. 4m + 6o
   B. 6m + 4o
   C. 10mo
   D. 3m + 6o

4. Change 9 m 5 cm to centimetres. (1 mark)
   A. 95 cm
   B. 14 cm
   C. 905 cm
   D. 9,050 cm

5. Which unit is best for measuring the length of a classroom? (1 mark)
   A. Centimetres only
   B. Metres
   C. Litres
   D. Kilograms

6. A rectangle is 20 cm long and 6 cm wide. What is its perimeter? (1 mark)
   A. 54 cm
   B. 52 cm
   C. 120 cm
   D. 26 cm

7. A rectangle has an area of 48 square units and 6 rows. How many columns does it have? (1 mark)
   A. 9
   B. 8
   C. 42
   D. 54

8. A square is covered with 10 rows of 10 unit squares. What is its area? (1 mark)
   A. 40 square units
   B. 100 square units
   C. 20 square units
   D. 110 square units

9. Rectangle P has 8 rows and 7 columns. Rectangle Q has 9 rows and 6 columns. Which has the bigger area? (1 mark)
   A. Rectangle Q
   B. They are equal
   C. Rectangle P
   D. It cannot be told

10. A cuboid is 2 blocks long, 2 blocks wide and 2 blocks high. What is its volume? (1 mark)
   A. 10 blocks
   B. 6 blocks
   C. 8 blocks
   D. 4 blocks

11. A cuboid is 3 blocks long, 3 blocks wide and 3 blocks high. What is its volume? (1 mark)
   A. 27 blocks
   B. 9 blocks
   C. 24 blocks
   D. 30 blocks

12. A cuboid is 6 blocks long, 4 blocks wide and 3 blocks high. What is its volume? (1 mark)
   A. 72 blocks
   B. 78 blocks
   C. 13 blocks
   D. 24 blocks

13. What is 5 L − 2 1/2 L? (1 mark)
   A. 2 3/4 L
   B. 3 L
   C. 2 1/2 L
   D. 2 1/4 L

14. What is 3 L − 1/4 L? (1 mark)
   A. 2 3/4 L
   B. 3 1/4 L
   C. 2 1/2 L
   D. 3 L

15. How many 1/4 kg masses balance a 1 kg mass? (1 mark)
   A. 2
   B. 4
   C. 8
   D. 3

16. What is 3 kg − 1 3/4 kg? (1 mark)
   A. 1 1/4 kg
   B. 1 kg
   C. 1 3/4 kg
   D. 1 1/2 kg

17. What should you check first before using a beam balance? (1 mark)
   A. That it is near a window
   B. That both pans are full
   C. That it has a 1 kg mass in each pan
   D. That the beam is level when both pans are empty

18. Change 96 hours to days. (1 mark)
   A. 5 days
   B. 8 days
   C. 1.6 days
   D. 4 days

19. How many hours are in 2 days? (1 mark)
   A. 48 hours
   B. 120 hours
   C. 72 hours
   D. 24 hours

20. What is 7 h 15 min − 3 h 50 min? (1 mark)
   A. 3 h 15 min
   B. 3 h 35 min
   C. 4 h 25 min
   D. 3 h 25 min

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Amina says the area of a rectangle with 4 rows and 6 columns is 10 because 4 + 6 = 10. Explain her mistake and give the correct area. (3 marks)

22. A 20 L jerrycan is used to fill 5 L buckets. How many buckets can be filled? How many 1/4 L cups can be filled from one bucket? (4 marks)

23. Amina says the perimeter of a rectangle 8 cm by 5 cm is 13 cm. Explain her mistake and give the correct perimeter. (3 marks)

24. Achieng buys 3 packets of flour of 1/2 kg each and 2 packets of sugar of 1 kg each. Find the total mass. (3 marks)

25. Explain why 2a + 3b cannot be written as 5ab. (2 marks)

26. A box is packed with cubes in layers. Each layer has 8 cubes along the length and 5 cubes across the width. There are 4 layers. (a) How many cubes are in one layer? (b) What is the volume of the packed cubes? (c) If 30 cubes are taken out, how many cubes are left? (5 marks)

27. Otieno is a years old and his sister is 3 years older. Write an expression for his sister's age and find her age if Otieno is 9. (3 marks)

28. Bags of 5 kg are filled from a 50 kg sack of rice. Find the number of bags. (2 marks)

29. Explain why you should read a measuring jug at the same height as the water. (2 marks)

30. Work out 6 1/4 kg − 2 3/4 kg. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — TERMLY EXAM #17 (TERM 2) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — 5y + 2
   Only like terms can be joined. 8y + 2 − 3y = 5y + 2.

2. B — 42
   Replace the letter by its value and work it out. The answer is 42.

3. A — 4m + 6o
   Only like terms can be joined. 3m + 2o + m + 4o = 4m + 6o.

4. C — 905 cm
   1 m = 100 cm. 9 × 100 = 900, and 900 + 5 = 905. So the answer is 905 cm.

5. B — Metres
   A classroom is several metres long, so metres are the sensible unit.

6. B — 52 cm
   Perimeter = 20 + 6 + 20 + 6 = 52 cm.

7. B — 8
   Rows × columns = 48, so columns = 48 ÷ 6 = 8.

8. B — 100 square units
   Area = 10 × 10 = 100 square units.

9. C — Rectangle P
   P = 8 × 7 = 56 and Q = 9 × 6 = 54. Rectangle P has the bigger area.

10. C — 8 blocks
   One layer has 2 × 2 = 4 blocks. There are 2 layers, so the volume is 4 × 2 = 8 blocks.

11. A — 27 blocks
   One layer has 3 × 3 = 9 blocks. There are 3 layers, so the volume is 9 × 3 = 27 blocks.

12. A — 72 blocks
   One layer has 6 × 4 = 24 blocks. There are 3 layers, so the volume is 24 × 3 = 72 blocks.

13. C — 2 1/2 L
   Work with the whole litres first and then the parts. 5 L − 2 1/2 L = 2 1/2 L.

14. A — 2 3/4 L
   Work with the whole litres first and then the parts. 3 L − 1/4 L = 2 3/4 L.

15. B — 4
   Four quarters make one whole kilogram.

16. A — 1 1/4 kg
   Work with the whole kilograms first and then the parts. 3 kg − 1 3/4 kg = 1 1/4 kg.

17. D — That the beam is level when both pans are empty
   The beam must be level when empty for the measurement to be correct.

18. D — 4 days
   96 ÷ 24 = 4 days.

19. A — 48 hours
   1 day = 24 hours, so 2 × 24 = 48 hours.

20. D — 3 h 25 min
   Change 1 hour to 60 minutes when the minutes are not enough. The answer is 3 h 25 min.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: She added the rows and columns. Area is rows × columns = 4 × 6 = 24 square units.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for saying she added, 1 mark for saying multiply, 1 mark for 24.

22. (4 marks)
   Answer: 4 buckets; 20 cups
   Working / marking points: 20 ÷ 5 = 4 (2 marks); 5 × 4 = 20 cups (2 marks).

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: She added only two sides. The perimeter is the distance all the way round, so we add all four sides: 8 + 5 + 8 + 5 = 26 cm.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the mistake, 1 mark for the reason, 1 mark for 26 cm.

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: 3 1/2 kg
   Working / marking points: 3 × 1/2 = 1 1/2 kg (1 mark); 2 × 1 = 2 kg (1 mark); total 3 1/2 kg (1 mark).

25. (2 marks)
   Answer: a and b are different, so 2a and 3b are not like terms and cannot be joined.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for unlike terms and 1 mark for the reason.

26. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) 40 cubes (b) 160 cubes (c) 130 cubes
   Working / marking points: (a) 8 × 5 = 40 (1 mark); (b) 40 × 4 = 160 (2 marks); (c) 160 − 30 = 130 (2 marks).

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: a + 3. When a = 9, her age is 12 years.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a + 3, 1 mark for replacing a by 9, 1 mark for 12 years.

28. (2 marks)
   Answer: 10 bags
   Working / marking points: 50 ÷ 5 = 10. 1 mark for the division and 1 mark for the answer.

29. (2 marks)
   Answer: Looking from above or below makes the water level seem to be at a different mark, so the reading would be wrong.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for saying the reading can be wrong and 1 mark for the reason.

30. (3 marks)
   Answer: 3 1/2 kg
   Working / marking points: Change 6 1/4 to 5 5/4 (1 mark); wholes 5 − 2 = 3 and quarters 5/4 − 3/4 = 1/2 (1 mark); answer 3 1/2 kg (1 mark).
